# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 29 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 29 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_029_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 3 — Truth

**1** Again he spoke to me: "Love truth, and let nothing but truth come out of your mouth, so that the spirit which God caused to dwell in this flesh may be found to be true by all, and so the Lord who dwells within you may be glorified. For the Lord is true in every word, and in him there is no falsehood. **2** Those therefore who lie renounce the Lord and defraud him, failing to return to him the deposit which they received. For they received from him a spirit free of all deceit. If they give it back full of lies, they have dishonored and defiled the deposit of the true Lord. **3** But those who practice truth continually will be pleasing to God and will live to God." **4** "And what of those who falsify and lie?" "They will have no life with God — unless they repent and turn from their lying and practice truth again. For those who repent of their lying are sanctified. Blessed are all the righteous who keep the Lord's commandments."

---

### Council Notes

Mandate 3 is the shortest mandate after Mandate 1, but introduces one of the Shepherd's most significant theological metaphors: the spirit of truth as a deposit (parathēkē) entrusted to humans.

The word parathēkē was a technical banking/legal term for goods held in trust. Using it for the indwelling Spirit creates a vivid image: God has deposited his own truthful spirit within each person; to return it corrupted with lies is a form of theft — defrauding the Depositor.

The parallel in 2 Timothy 1:14 ("guard the good deposit, with the help of the Holy Spirit") confirms this was a live early Christian concept.

The final beatitude ("blessed are all the righteous who keep the Lord's commandments") echoes Psalm 119 and the beatitude tradition, providing a liturgical closure to the mandate.
